start = 0

for i,(s,e) in enumerate(stripes):

"**Wake Me Up**" (sometimes listed as "**Wake Me Up!**") is a song by Swedish DJ and record producer [Avicii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avicii "Avicii"). It was released as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from his debut album *[True](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_\(Avicii_album\) "True (Avicii album)")* on 17 June 2013, by [PRMD Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRMD_Music "PRMD Music") and [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records"). It was written by Avicii, [Mike Einziger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Einziger "Mike Einziger") of [Incubus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incubus_\(band\) "Incubus (band)"), and American [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") singer [Aloe Blacc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aloe_Blacc "Aloe Blacc"), who provides vocals for the track.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) [Mike Einziger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Einziger "Mike Einziger") provides acoustic guitar, while Peter Dyer provides keyboard on the song.

Avicii introduced "Wake Me Up" for the first time live on stage at the [Ultra Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_Music_Festival "Ultra Music Festival") in Miami. The experimental rendering (it was accompanied by a live band with instruments and vocalists, including Blacc, Einziger and Incubus members [Ben Kenney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Kenney "Ben Kenney") on bass and [José Pasillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/José_Pasillas "José Pasillas") on drums)[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) reportedly confused and angered a section of the electronic dance festival community.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) Subsequently, Avicii achieved critical and commercial success with the release of the single worldwide.

"Wake Me Up" has been named as the highest charting dance track of the 2010s,[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) sitting at number 13 in the 100-strong list from the official UK Singles Chart. It is the only song to crack the *Billboard* Decade-End without making the top three during any week.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) It also reached number one in much of Europe and charted well in various countries.

The song has been described as a "summer anthem"[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) by *Variance Magazine* and, throughout the 2013 festival season, Avicii included it as part of the opening or closing sequence of his sets at EDC Las Vegas, EDC London, [Tomorrowland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomorrowland_\(festival\) "Tomorrowland (festival)"), [Creamfields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creamfields "Creamfields"), [Electric Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_Zoo "Electric Zoo") and the [iTunes Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes_Festival "ITunes Festival").[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) Due to the success of the song, Blacc later released an acoustic version of "Wake Me Up" in his solo EP *[Wake Me Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_\(EP\) "Wake Me Up (EP)")*. It was also released as a promotional stand-alone single on [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"), made available online for downloads via [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes"). A separate music video was also made. The Blacc single charted on various charts.

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

In an interview with the *[Daily Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_Star_\(United_Kingdom\) "Daily Star (United Kingdom)")*, Avicii, who had previously labelled "Wake Me Up!" as "a fun experiment" during an exclusive chat with [MTV UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_\(British_and_Irish_TV_channel\) "MTV (British and Irish TV channel)"),[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) said: "I had a demo with [Mac Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Davis "Mac Davis") singing, the guy who wrote some songs that were covered by [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), but I needed another singer to do the parts. At the same time I was tipped off about doing another track with [Aloe Blacc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aloe_Blacc "Aloe Blacc"), and I started working on that track. When I was with [Mike Einziger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Einziger "Mike Einziger") from [Incubus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incubus_\(band\) "Incubus (band)"), we came up with the chord progression and the melody for 'Wake Me Up!' but no real lyrics. None of us sing and we really needed to get that demo down and the only person I knew that lived in [LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") was Aloe, so I called him and he was free. Lyrics come really easy to him so he wrote them in a couple of hours and we finished the track."[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

Aloe Blacc, who is not credited on the track, explained to *[The Huffington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Huffington_Post "The Huffington Post")*: "I started writing the lyrics at the top of 2013, travelling back from [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland"). I started in [hip hop music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") back in the 90s and I never expected to be singing and have an actual career as a musician, but I'm travelling all over the world and I thought 'Life is a dream, wake me up when it's all over'. I was invited to the studio with Avicii and Mike Einziger from Incubus, and when I got to the studio they had already come up with a chord progression of the song. I came in with the lyrics and I just developed the melody as I heard the chords, and we all thought it was something very strong. We finished the song that night as an acoustic version, then Avicii made the dance mix in a couple of days, and that's what we released to the world, and that was his release." Blacc later released an acoustic version[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) of the song which was included on his solo EP *[Wake Me Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_\(EP\) "Wake Me Up (EP)")*. It was also released as a promotional stand-alone single by [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") and made available online for download via [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes"). The single also charted in its own right in various charts.

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")\]

"Wake Me Up" is a [folktronica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folktronica "Folktronica") song,[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) blending elements of [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music"), [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music").[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) Musically, it is written in the key of [B minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B_minor "B minor") and runs at 124 beats per minute (BPM). It follows a chord progression of Bm/G/D/A – Bm/G/D/F#, with Blacc's vocals ranging from B2 to B4.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Robert Copsey of *[Digital Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Spy "Digital Spy")* gave the song a positive review, stating:

> "As chart-friendly [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") continues to reach the furthest corners of the globe, staying ahead of the pack can prove a tricky task – especially when more and more acts arrive on the scene turning out mixes with identikit build-ups, tired lyrics and uninspired breakdowns that newcomers to the arena lap up with excitement. Kudos to Avicii then, who has dared to try something a little different for his latest offering. "So wake me up when it's all over/ When I'm wiser and I'm older," featured artist Aloe Blacc sings over dialled-up, country-flecked guitar strums that sound like [Mumford & Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumford_&_Sons "Mumford & Sons") on speed. The jig-along chorus may conjure up images of Brits-on-tour, but to be honest, what summer anthem doesn't?" ![Star](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Star_empty.svg/20px-Star_empty.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail).[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

At the end of the year, *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* listed "Wake Me Up" at number 26 on its list of 100 Best Songs of 2013\.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

The single has peaked at number one in 22 countries to date, including Australia, New Zealand, Hungary, Ireland,[\[20\]](#cite_note-:0-20) the United Kingdom and several European countries, in addition to reaching the top 10 in six others. The song is also the most searched on the [Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc "Apple Inc") owned music identifying app [Shazam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_\(music_app\) "Shazam (music app)") with more than 23 million in February 2018\.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

In Australia, the song debuted at number 42 on 24 June. Two weeks later it reached the top spot, making it both Avicii's and Blacc's highest-charting single in the country.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\] On its sixth week at the top, 12 August, "Wake Me Up" became the longest-running number one by a Swedish act since [Roxette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxette "Roxette")'s 1989 hit "[The Look](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Look "The Look")".[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) In Ireland, "Wake Me Up" spent seven consecutive weeks at number one.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) "Wake Me Up!" has performed well in the North American music markets, having peaked in Canada and the United States at number two and number four, respectively. It spent 21 weeks in the top ten of the Billboard Hot 100, and 54 non-consecutive weeks overall, making it the first Dance/Electronic song to stay over a year on that chart. It also reached number one position in the 7 September 2013 issue of Billboard's [Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay") Chart.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) In Canada it was the second best-selling song of 2013 with 519,000 copies sold (523,000 for all versions combined).[\[25\]](#cite_note-canada_sales-25) It is the first dance/electronic song to sell over 4 million copies in the U.S.,[\[26\]](#cite_note-26) and as of August 2015 it has sold over 4,060,000 copies.[\[27\]](#cite_note-yahoo_sales-27)

In July 2013, "Wake Me Up" entered at the number one on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"), becoming Avicii's second UK number one and selling 88,000 copies in its first day[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) and 267,000 in its first week, becoming Britain's fastest-selling single of 2013 at the time of writing.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) Following three weeks at number one, "Wake Me Up" spent a further four consecutive weeks at number two, and a total of 11 consecutive weeks in the top ten.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) By October 2013, the single had sold over 1 million copies in the UK, becoming the 140th single to do so in UK chart history and the third single of 2013 to do so.[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) "Wake Me Up" was also the fifth most streamed track of 2013 in the UK.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) The song also spent nine consecutive weeks at number one on the [UK Dance Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Dance_Chart "UK Dance Chart") until being replaced by Avicii's next single "[You Make Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Make_Me "You Make Me")".\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

## Music videos

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Music videos")\]

A lyric video to accompany the release of "Wake Me Up" was first released on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") 28 June 2013, at a total length of four minutes and thirty two seconds, and teaser clips for the official video were also released.

The official video for the song was released a month after the lyric video on 29 July. It was directed by celebrity photographer [Mark Seliger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Seliger "Mark Seliger") and co-directed and edited by CB "Barney" Miller (former guitarist for 1980's pop band [Miller Miller Miller & Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miller_Miller_Miller_&_Sloan "Miller Miller Miller & Sloan")). It features a woman and a young girl, intended to be sisters, portrayed respectively by Russian model [Kristina Romanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristina_Romanova "Kristina Romanova") and Laneya Grace. It depicts them and how they are different from the people in their dreary village, as Laneya mentioned that people are seen looking at the two often with disgust and revulsion except for one of them. One morning, Kristina gets up early and rides off on a horse to a nearby city. Once in the city, she finds how welcoming and accepting the people are of her. She notices a woman with the Avicii logo birthmark like the one on her lower arm. They meet others and then jump into a truck and are then shown to be attending an Avicii concert. The next morning, Kristina rides back home on the horse and tells Laneya that she found "somewhere \[they\] belong" as they pack up all their belongings and depart the village for good. The video ends with them walking down the highway as they move into the city and shots from the concert and one of the staring villagers from the beginning seeming to notice and depressed by the sisters' departure before resuming her uninspired life.

The video includes [product placement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_placement "Product placement") from Denim & Supply by [Ralph Lauren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Lauren_Corporation "Ralph Lauren Corporation") and the [Sony Xperia Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Xperia_Z "Sony Xperia Z") smartphone, used to capture a group [selfie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selfie "Selfie") at the concert. The video was shot by the [Santa Clara River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clara_River_\(California\) "Santa Clara River (California)") orange groves, in the town of [Piru, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piru,_California "Piru, California"), northwest of [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), and [Downtown LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_LA "Downtown LA") as well as concert footage from an Avicii performing at the 2013 Ultra Music Festival in Miami. As of January 2025, the video has 2\.4 billion views on Avicii's official YouTube channel,[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) making it one of the 60 [most viewed videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos") on the site.

In addition, his own channel Avicii collaborated with the YouTube channel "Yo Mama" to produce the official music video for the single on his remix album, *True: Avicii By Avicii*.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) It was directed by Zachary James and Alex Negrete.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)

"**Wake Me Up**" (sometimes listed as "**Wake Me Up!**") is a song by Swedish DJ and record producer [Avicii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avicii "Avicii"). It was released as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from his debut album *[True](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_\(Avicii_album\) "True (Avicii album)")* on 17 June 2013, by [PRMD Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRMD_Music "PRMD Music") and [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records"). It was written by Avicii, [Mike Einziger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Einziger "Mike Einziger") of [Incubus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incubus_\(band\) "Incubus (band)"), and American [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") singer [Aloe Blacc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aloe_Blacc "Aloe Blacc"), who provides vocals for the track.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) [Mike Einziger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Einziger "Mike Einziger") provides acoustic guitar, while Peter Dyer provides keyboard on the song.

Avicii introduced "Wake Me Up" for the first time live on stage at the [Ultra Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_Music_Festival "Ultra Music Festival") in Miami. The experimental rendering (it was accompanied by a live band with instruments and vocalists, including Blacc, Einziger and Incubus members [Ben Kenney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Kenney "Ben Kenney") on bass and [José Pasillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/José_Pasillas "José Pasillas") on drums)[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) reportedly confused and angered a section of the electronic dance festival community.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) Subsequently, Avicii achieved critical and commercial success with the release of the single worldwide.

"Wake Me Up" has been named as the highest charting dance track of the 2010s,[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) sitting at number 13 in the 100-strong list from the official UK Singles Chart. It is the only song to crack the *Billboard* Decade-End without making the top three during any week.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) It also reached number one in much of Europe and charted well in various countries.

The song has been described as a "summer anthem"[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) by *Variance Magazine* and, throughout the 2013 festival season, Avicii included it as part of the opening or closing sequence of his sets at EDC Las Vegas, EDC London, [Tomorrowland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomorrowland_\(festival\) "Tomorrowland (festival)"), [Creamfields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creamfields "Creamfields"), [Electric Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_Zoo "Electric Zoo") and the [iTunes Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes_Festival "ITunes Festival").[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) Due to the success of the song, Blacc later released an acoustic version of "Wake Me Up" in his solo EP *[Wake Me Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_\(EP\) "Wake Me Up (EP)")*. It was also released as a promotional stand-alone single on [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"), made available online for downloads via [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes"). A separate music video was also made. The Blacc single charted on various charts.

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

In an interview with the *[Daily Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_Star_\(United_Kingdom\) "Daily Star (United Kingdom)")*, Avicii, who had previously labelled "Wake Me Up!" as "a fun experiment" during an exclusive chat with [MTV UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_\(British_and_Irish_TV_channel\) "MTV (British and Irish TV channel)"),[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) said: "I had a demo with [Mac Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Davis "Mac Davis") singing, the guy who wrote some songs that were covered by [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley"), but I needed another singer to do the parts. At the same time I was tipped off about doing another track with [Aloe Blacc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aloe_Blacc "Aloe Blacc"), and I started working on that track. When I was with [Mike Einziger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Einziger "Mike Einziger") from [Incubus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incubus_\(band\) "Incubus (band)"), we came up with the chord progression and the melody for 'Wake Me Up!' but no real lyrics. None of us sing and we really needed to get that demo down and the only person I knew that lived in [LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") was Aloe, so I called him and he was free. Lyrics come really easy to him so he wrote them in a couple of hours and we finished the track."[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

Aloe Blacc, who is not credited on the track, explained to *[The Huffington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Huffington_Post "The Huffington Post")*: "I started writing the lyrics at the top of 2013, travelling back from [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland"). I started in [hip hop music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") back in the 90s and I never expected to be singing and have an actual career as a musician, but I'm travelling all over the world and I thought 'Life is a dream, wake me up when it's all over'. I was invited to the studio with Avicii and Mike Einziger from Incubus, and when I got to the studio they had already come up with a chord progression of the song. I came in with the lyrics and I just developed the melody as I heard the chords, and we all thought it was something very strong. We finished the song that night as an acoustic version, then Avicii made the dance mix in a couple of days, and that's what we released to the world, and that was his release." Blacc later released an acoustic version[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) of the song which was included on his solo EP *[Wake Me Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_\(EP\) "Wake Me Up (EP)")*. It was also released as a promotional stand-alone single by [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") and made available online for download via [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes"). The single also charted in its own right in various charts.

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition")\]

"Wake Me Up" is a [folktronica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folktronica "Folktronica") song,[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) blending elements of [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music"), [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music").[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) Musically, it is written in the key of [B minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B_minor "B minor") and runs at 124 beats per minute (BPM). It follows a chord progression of Bm/G/D/A – Bm/G/D/F#, with Blacc's vocals ranging from B2 to B4.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Robert Copsey of *[Digital Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Spy "Digital Spy")* gave the song a positive review, stating:

> "As chart-friendly [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") continues to reach the furthest corners of the globe, staying ahead of the pack can prove a tricky task – especially when more and more acts arrive on the scene turning out mixes with identikit build-ups, tired lyrics and uninspired breakdowns that newcomers to the arena lap up with excitement. Kudos to Avicii then, who has dared to try something a little different for his latest offering. "So wake me up when it's all over/ When I'm wiser and I'm older," featured artist Aloe Blacc sings over dialled-up, country-flecked guitar strums that sound like [Mumford & Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumford_&_Sons "Mumford & Sons") on speed. The jig-along chorus may conjure up images of Brits-on-tour, but to be honest, what summer anthem doesn't?" ![Star](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Star_empty.svg/20px-Star_empty.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail).[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

At the end of the year, *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* listed "Wake Me Up" at number 26 on its list of 100 Best Songs of 2013\.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

The single has peaked at number one in 22 countries to date, including Australia, New Zealand, Hungary, Ireland,[\[20\]](#cite_note-:0-20) the United Kingdom and several European countries, in addition to reaching the top 10 in six others. The song is also the most searched on the [Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc "Apple Inc") owned music identifying app [Shazam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_\(music_app\) "Shazam (music app)") with more than 23 million in February 2018\.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

In Australia, the song debuted at number 42 on 24 June. Two weeks later it reached the top spot, making it both Avicii's and Blacc's highest-charting single in the country.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\] On its sixth week at the top, 12 August, "Wake Me Up" became the longest-running number one by a Swedish act since [Roxette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxette "Roxette")'s 1989 hit "[The Look](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Look "The Look")".[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) In Ireland, "Wake Me Up" spent seven consecutive weeks at number one.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) "Wake Me Up!" has performed well in the North American music markets, having peaked in Canada and the United States at number two and number four, respectively. It spent 21 weeks in the top ten of the Billboard Hot 100, and 54 non-consecutive weeks overall, making it the first Dance/Electronic song to stay over a year on that chart. It also reached number one position in the 7 September 2013 issue of Billboard's [Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay") Chart.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) In Canada it was the second best-selling song of 2013 with 519,000 copies sold (523,000 for all versions combined).[\[25\]](#cite_note-canada_sales-25) It is the first dance/electronic song to sell over 4 million copies in the U.S.,[\[26\]](#cite_note-26) and as of August 2015 it has sold over 4,060,000 copies.[\[27\]](#cite_note-yahoo_sales-27)

In July 2013, "Wake Me Up" entered at the number one on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"), becoming Avicii's second UK number one and selling 88,000 copies in its first day[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) and 267,000 in its first week, becoming Britain's fastest-selling single of 2013 at the time of writing.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) Following three weeks at number one, "Wake Me Up" spent a further four consecutive weeks at number two, and a total of 11 consecutive weeks in the top ten.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) By October 2013, the single had sold over 1 million copies in the UK, becoming the 140th single to do so in UK chart history and the third single of 2013 to do so.[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) "Wake Me Up" was also the fifth most streamed track of 2013 in the UK.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) The song also spent nine consecutive weeks at number one on the [UK Dance Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Dance_Chart "UK Dance Chart") until being replaced by Avicii's next single "[You Make Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Make_Me "You Make Me")".\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

## Music videos

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Wake_Me_Up_\(Avicii_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Music videos")\]

A lyric video to accompany the release of "Wake Me Up" was first released on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") 28 June 2013, at a total length of four minutes and thirty two seconds, and teaser clips for the official video were also released.

The official video for the song was released a month after the lyric video on 29 July. It was directed by celebrity photographer [Mark Seliger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Seliger "Mark Seliger") and co-directed and edited by CB "Barney" Miller (former guitarist for 1980's pop band [Miller Miller Miller & Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miller_Miller_Miller_&_Sloan "Miller Miller Miller & Sloan")). It features a woman and a young girl, intended to be sisters, portrayed respectively by Russian model [Kristina Romanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristina_Romanova "Kristina Romanova") and Laneya Grace. It depicts them and how they are different from the people in their dreary village, as Laneya mentioned that people are seen looking at the two often with disgust and revulsion except for one of them. One morning, Kristina gets up early and rides off on a horse to a nearby city. Once in the city, she finds how welcoming and accepting the people are of her. She notices a woman with the Avicii logo birthmark like the one on her lower arm. They meet others and then jump into a truck and are then shown to be attending an Avicii concert. The next morning, Kristina rides back home on the horse and tells Laneya that she found "somewhere \[they\] belong" as they pack up all their belongings and depart the village for good. The video ends with them walking down the highway as they move into the city and shots from the concert and one of the staring villagers from the beginning seeming to notice and depressed by the sisters' departure before resuming her uninspired life.

The video includes [product placement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_placement "Product placement") from Denim & Supply by [Ralph Lauren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Lauren_Corporation "Ralph Lauren Corporation") and the [Sony Xperia Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Xperia_Z "Sony Xperia Z") smartphone, used to capture a group [selfie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selfie "Selfie") at the concert. The video was shot by the [Santa Clara River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clara_River_\(California\) "Santa Clara River (California)") orange groves, in the town of [Piru, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piru,_California "Piru, California"), northwest of [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), and [Downtown LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_LA "Downtown LA") as well as concert footage from an Avicii performing at the 2013 Ultra Music Festival in Miami. As of January 2025, the video has 2\.4 billion views on Avicii's official YouTube channel,[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) making it one of the 60 [most viewed videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos") on the site.

In addition, his own channel Avicii collaborated with the YouTube channel "Yo Mama" to produce the official music video for the single on his remix album, *True: Avicii By Avicii*.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) It was directed by Zachary James and Alex Negrete.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)

"**Closer**" is a song by American DJ duo [the Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chainsmokers "The Chainsmokers") featuring American singer [Halsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halsey_\(singer\) "Halsey (singer)"). Halsey duets with Chainsmokers member Andrew Taggart,[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) who had never provided lead vocals on a song before (although he provided background vocals for "[Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roses_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Roses (The Chainsmokers song)")"). It was released on July 29, 2016, through [Disruptor Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disruptor_Records "Disruptor Records") and [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records").[\[5\]](#cite_note-iTunes_Store_Worldwide-5) The song was written by Taggart, Halsey, [Shaun Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Frank "Shaun Frank"), [Freddy Kennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_the_Child_\(band\) "Louis the Child (band)"), [Isaac Slade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Slade "Isaac Slade") and [Joe King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_King_\(guitarist\) "Joe King (guitarist)"). Halsey's vocals were produced by [DJ Swivel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Swivel "DJ Swivel"),[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) while the main song production was handled by the Chainsmokers as usual. Musically, it is a [future bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_bass "Future bass") and [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop") song with a "[retro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro_\(music\) "Retro (music)")" style synthesizer in the chorus. Taggart and Halsey take turns singing their parts before singing the chorus together as the song concludes. The song is also included on the Japanese edition of The Chainsmokers' debut studio album, *[Memories...Do Not Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memories...Do_Not_Open "Memories...Do Not Open")* (2017).

In the United States, "Closer" became both the Chainsmokers' and Halsey's first number one single on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). The song stayed at the top spot for 12 consecutive weeks; it was the highest-charting [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") song to crack the *Billboard* Decade-End in the 2010s according to *Billboard*. The Chainsmokers became the first act to have four songs ("Closer" being the fourth) that top the [Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Electronic_Songs "Dance/Electronic Songs") chart, passing [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris"), who held the previous record with three. Internationally the single topped the charts in seventeen countries including Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Ireland, and the United Kingdom, making it both the Chainsmokers' and Halsey's first chart-topping song in all six countries. The song went on to become the first song to spend 26 weeks in the top five of the *Billboard* Hot 100 chart.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) It also became the second song in the history of the Hot 100 chart to spend 32 weeks in the top ten of the chart.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

The song was performed live for the first time at the Number Fest Concert at [Ohio University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_University "Ohio University") on Saturday April 16, 2016\.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) The Chainsmokers performed “Closer” for the second time at [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_\(festival\) "Coachella (festival)") on Sunday, April 17, 2016\. Halsey and the Chainsmokers performed the track live at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards") as well as a remix of the song at the 2016 [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"). Its music video was released on October 24, 2016\.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It received a nomination for [Best Pop Duo/Group Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Duo/Group_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance") at the [2017 Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards").

In 2018, the song received a diamond certification by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") for selling 10 million units in the United States, later being certified 18× Platinum in 2026\.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) In 2023, the Chainsmokers collaborated with Japanese rock star [Yoshiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoshiki_\(musician\) "Yoshiki (musician)") to perform a classical version of "Closer" in the documentary film *[Yoshiki: Under the Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoshiki:_Under_the_Sky "Yoshiki: Under the Sky")*.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

The song's beat was created in a session between Chainsmokers member Andrew Taggart and Freddy Kennett of [Louis the Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_the_Child_\(band\) "Louis the Child (band)"). Taggart wrote the song with Canadian DJ [Shaun Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Frank "Shaun Frank") in one session, and Frank encouraged him to sing on the song. According to Taggart, the track was inspired by the [Blink-182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182 "Blink-182") song "[I Miss You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Miss_You_\(Blink-182_song\) "I Miss You (Blink-182 song)")", which the duo were listening to on repeat and is referenced in the song.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Lauren_Nostro-15) He later said the song instead was "[Feeling This](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feeling_This "Feeling This")", though he could not really remember which: "I've listened to their [self-titled album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182_\(album\) "Blink-182 (album)") so many times the whole thing is pretty much beat," he tweeted.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) The band [Taking Back Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taking_Back_Sunday "Taking Back Sunday") also influenced the song.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Lauren_Nostro-15) The song is about a couple who broke up and unexpectedly meet long after, leading to romantic attraction again.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) Before [Halsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halsey_\(singer\) "Halsey (singer)") was brought on as the female vocalist, the collaboration was originally supposed to feature former [Fifth Harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Harmony "Fifth Harmony") member [Camila Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Cabello "Camila Cabello").[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

The song was mixed by [Jordan Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Swivel "DJ Swivel") who also oversaw the recording of the guest vocal.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

After comparisons were drawn between "Closer" and [The Fray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fray "The Fray")'s "[Over My Head (Cable Car)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Over_My_Head_\(Cable_Car\) "Over My Head (Cable Car)")", lead singer [Isaac Slade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Slade "Isaac Slade") and guitarist [Joe King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_King_\(guitarist\) "Joe King (guitarist)") of The Fray were credited as co-writers of "Closer" on September 2, 2016\.[\[20\]](#cite_note-Fekadu-20) The song was released on July 29, 2016, through [Disruptor Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disruptor_Records "Disruptor Records") and [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"). [Genius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genius_\(website\) "Genius (website)") pointed out the similarity between "Closer" and [Fetty Wap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetty_Wap "Fetty Wap")'s "[679](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/679_\(song\) "679 (song)")" in September 2016, claiming that the songs' choruses are nearly identical, with the only major difference being that Fetty's is in D major and The Chainsmokers' is in A-flat major. Genius even cut together a video of the choruses playing over each other.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

## Composition and lyrics

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition and lyrics")\]

The song is written in the key of [A-flat major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-flat_major "A-flat major") with a [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time") tempo of 95 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute") and a chord progression of D♭(9)–E♭6add4–Fm7–E♭. The vocals span from E♭2 to B♭5.[\[22\]](#cite_note-Musicnotes-22)

The title of the song comes from part of the main hook: the singer asks his lover to "pull them *closer*" in the car's backseat. The words to the song speak to "youth" and "heartbreak".[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) The song makes references to [Range Rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_Rover "Range Rover") vehicles, the cities of [Boulder, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulder,_Colorado "Boulder, Colorado"), [Tucson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona "Tucson, Arizona"), [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona") and the band [Blink-182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182 "Blink-182").[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) It talks about being broke and passionate.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

[Matt Medved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Medved "Matt Medved") of *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* wrote the song "sounds like an instant classic," stating that it "\[boasts\] an earworm chorus and evocative verses like 'play that [Blink-182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182 "Blink-182") song that we beat to death in [Tucson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona "Tucson, Arizona"),' (one of Halsey's few solo verses), "Closer" captures the [millennial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials "Millennials") [zeitgeist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeitgeist "Zeitgeist") in brilliantly infectious fashion."[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") journalist Deepa Lakshmin called the song "an upbeat, dance-worthy jam that deserves a spot on your summer playlist. It'll make you forget about all your pesky life problems and live in the moment."[\[26\]](#cite_note-26) The song received a more mixed review from *[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")*, with a consensus from various editors resulting in a 5/10 rating.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) While reviewing Halsey's 2021 album *[If I Can't Have Love, I Want Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Can't_Have_Love,_I_Want_Power "If I Can't Have Love, I Want Power")*, Dani Blum of *[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")* described their[\[note 1\]](#cite_note-28) "[Auto-Tuned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auto-Tune "Auto-Tune")" part of the song as the "ache \[...\] that threatened to define their career."[\[28\]](#cite_note-29)

*[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* ranked "Closer" at number 29 on their "100 Best Pop Songs of 2016" list: "The year's longest-running No. 1 on the Hot 100 was as predictable a smash as they come: Perfectly played duet drama, an immediately recognizable hook – maybe a little too instantly recognizable – and a Blink-182 reference that made every Millennial listening nod with begrudging respect. Overplay might've done The Chainsmokers and Halsey a temporary disservice, but just wait for the emotional rush that hits in 2025 when you're hanging in a hotel bar and hear this for the first time in years."[\[29\]](#cite_note-30)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Calvin_Harris_-_Rock_in_Rio_Madrid_2012_-_09.jpg/250px-Calvin_Harris_-_Rock_in_Rio_Madrid_2012_-_09.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Calvin_Harris_-_Rock_in_Rio_Madrid_2012_-_09.jpg)

[Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") (*pictured*) had three songs that topped *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")*'s [Hot Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Dance/Electronic_Songs "Hot Dance/Electronic Songs") chart; "Closer" became the Chainsmoker's fourth song to do so and break the record.

"Closer" debuted at number nine on the *Billboard* Hot 100 in the issue dated August 20, 2016\.[\[30\]](#cite_note-31) It became the third top ten single for the Chainsmokers on the chart, after "[Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roses_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Roses (The Chainsmokers song)")" and "[Don't Let Me Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Let_Me_Down_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Don't Let Me Down (The Chainsmokers song)")". It is Halsey's first top ten on the chart and their second top forty. In the issue dated September 3, 2016, the song moved from number six to one, becoming both artists' first number-one song and the first song by a duo to top the chart since [Macklemore & Ryan Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macklemore_&_Ryan_Lewis "Macklemore & Ryan Lewis")' "[Thrift Shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrift_Shop "Thrift Shop")" and "[Can't Hold Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Hold_Us "Can't Hold Us")" in 2013\.[\[31\]](#cite_note-YM1-32)[\[32\]](#cite_note-Billboard1-33) It is also the first song titled "Closer" to reach number one ([Ne-Yo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ne-Yo "Ne-Yo")'s [song of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(Ne-Yo_song\) "Closer (Ne-Yo song)") reached number 7 in 2008). Moreover, the song also topped the [Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Electronic_Songs "Dance/Electronic Songs") chart, becoming the first song to reach number one on both the Hot 100 and the Dance/Electronic chart simultaneously since [Baauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baauer "Baauer")'s "[Harlem Shake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem_Shake_\(song\) "Harlem Shake (song)")" in early 2013\.[\[31\]](#cite_note-YM1-32) It became the duo's fourth number one song to top the latter chart, passing [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris")' previous record of three songs.[\[32\]](#cite_note-Billboard1-33) It went on to top the Hot 100 chart for twelve consecutive weeks.[\[33\]](#cite_note-34)

On the issue date November 5, 2016, "Closer" became the 33rd song to top the chart for at least 10 weeks. By spending an 11th week atop the chart, it became the longest number one single of 2016 surpassing [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)")'s "[One Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Dance "One Dance")" which spent 10 non-consecutive weeks at number one. In its fourth week, the song was joined by [Twenty One Pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty_One_Pilots "Twenty One Pilots")' "[Heathens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heathens_\(Twenty_One_Pilots_song\) "Heathens (Twenty One Pilots song)")", which moved from number three to number two. This marks the first time (and the third time overall) that duos have held the top two spots at the same time since June 1985, when [Tears for Fears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tears_for_Fears "Tears for Fears") was on top with "[Everybody Wants to Rule the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody_Wants_to_Rule_the_World "Everybody Wants to Rule the World")" and [Wham!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wham! "Wham!") was number two with "[Everything She Wants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everything_She_Wants "Everything She Wants")." (The week before, the two songs were in the opposite order.)[\[34\]](#cite_note-YM-35) On the chart issue dated November 26, 2016, the song was ousted from number one by "[Black Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Beatles "Black Beatles")" by [Rae Sremmurd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rae_Sremmurd "Rae Sremmurd") featuring [Gucci Mane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gucci_Mane "Gucci Mane"). On the issue dated January 28, 2017, "Closer" surpassed [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[Love Yourself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Yourself "Love Yourself")" for the most weeks logged in the top 10 from a song's debut, having totaled all 32 of its weeks on the chart in the region since its debut on the issue dated August 20, 2016\.[\[35\]](#cite_note-36)

On the issue dated March 11, 2017, "Closer" became the 4th song to stay in the top ten for 30 weeks. Only [Leann Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leann_Rimes "Leann Rimes")' "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")", [Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santana_\(band\) "Santana (band)")'s 1999 single "[Smooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_\(Santana_song\) "Smooth (Santana song)")" (feat. [Rob Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Thomas_\(musician\) "Rob Thomas (musician)")) and [Mark Ronson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ronson "Mark Ronson")'s "[Uptown Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")" (feat. [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars")) have achieved this feat since the *Billboard* Hot 100 was formed in 1958\. On the issue dated March 25, 2017, "Closer" spent its 32nd week in the top ten, tying [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes")' all-time record with "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")", before finally dropping out the following week. The record was broken later that year by [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran")'s "[Shape of You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shape_of_You "Shape of You")", which spent 33 consecutive weeks in the top ten.[\[36\]](#cite_note-37) The song's long run within the top 10 caused it to place at number 7 on [*Billboard'*s 2017 year-end chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2017 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2017") after placing at number 10 [the previous year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2016 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2016"), making "Closer" one of only four songs in the history of the chart to be ranked on the top ten of two separate Hot 100 year-end charts, along with [Chubby Checker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chubby_Checker "Chubby Checker")'s "[The Twist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twist_\(song\) "The Twist (song)")" (#10 in 1960 and \#9 in 1962), [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John")'s "[Candle in the Wind 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind_1997 "Candle in the Wind 1997")" (#1 in 1997 and \#8 in 1998), and [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes")' "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")" (#9 in 1997 and \#5 in 1998).

"Closer" achieved its 12th week atop [Digital Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") with 84,000 downloads sold in the week ending October 27, according to Nielsen Music; the total is the lowest for a number one song on the tally in 10 years.[\[37\]](#cite_note-ussales-38) The track became the third best-selling song of the year, behind [Flo Rida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flo_Rida "Flo Rida")'s "[My House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_House_\(Flo_Rida_song\) "My House (Flo Rida song)")" and [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake")'s "[Can't Stop the Feeling!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Stop_the_Feeling! "Can't Stop the Feeling!")".[\[38\]](#cite_note-sales-39)

Internationally, the song reached number one in Australia on August 13, 2016, also becoming both the Chainsmokers' and Halsey's first number-one song there.[\[39\]](#cite_note-AUS-40) It also peaked at number one in the UK, New Zealand and Canada. The song topped the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") for four weeks, becoming the first song by a duo to log multiple weeks at number one in both the US and the UK since [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO "LMFAO")'s "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")" in 2011\.[\[34\]](#cite_note-YM-35)

"Closer" is currently the [fifteenth most streamed song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_streamed_songs_on_Spotify "List of most streamed songs on Spotify") on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"). On May 19, 2017, it became only the second song to achieve 1 billion streams on the streaming platform. In April 2021, "Closer" surpassed 2 billion streams on Spotify, making it the sixth song to do so.[\[40\]](#cite_note-41)

## Lyric video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Lyric video")\]

The [lyric video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyric_video "Lyric video") for "Closer" was edited and directed by [Rory Kramer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rory_Kramer "Rory Kramer"), and features Alyssa Lynch and Jordan Wright. It received one billion views on January 10, 2017, and two billion views on February 4, 2018, making it the first lyric video ever to reach these milestones. As of January 2026, it has received over 3\.3 billion views, and is among the [fifty most-viewed videos of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos").[\[41\]](#cite_note-42)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Music video")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/3/34/ScreenshotCloser.jpg/250px-ScreenshotCloser.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ScreenshotCloser.jpg)

Andrew Taggart and Halsey in a scene of the official music video for "Closer."

The music video for "Closer", directed by [Dano Cerny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dano_Cerny "Dano Cerny"),[\[42\]](#cite_note-43) was released on October 24, 2016\. The video begins with the Chainsmokers' Andrew Taggart looking at Halsey while at a party. It then flashes back to an earlier time where Taggart and Halsey's characters met for the first time in a party, where they eventually ended up kissing in a kitchen. Through the video, Halsey and Taggart are seen singing, with Halsey in bra and panties and Taggart shirtless, with both in bed.

The video ends with Halsey leaving the party in present time, Taggart follows them outside and Halsey stops and turns around to see Taggart. They both look at each other, implying they regret drifting apart.

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

The Chainsmokers invited Halsey to the stage during their set at the Bonnaroo Music Festival to perform "Closer" for the first time in June 2016\.[\[43\]](#cite_note-44) Halsey and Taggart also performed the song live when they closed the show at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards").[\[44\]](#cite_note-45) The Chainsmokers and Halsey also performed "Closer" at the American Music Awards on November 20, 2016\.

## Remix

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Remix")\]

The official remix features American rapper [Wiz Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiz_Khalifa "Wiz Khalifa"). It was released online on March 17, 2017\.[\[45\]](#cite_note-46)

"**Closer**" is a song by American DJ duo [the Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chainsmokers "The Chainsmokers") featuring American singer [Halsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halsey_\(singer\) "Halsey (singer)"). Halsey duets with Chainsmokers member Andrew Taggart,[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) who had never provided lead vocals on a song before (although he provided background vocals for "[Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roses_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Roses (The Chainsmokers song)")"). It was released on July 29, 2016, through [Disruptor Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disruptor_Records "Disruptor Records") and [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records").[\[5\]](#cite_note-iTunes_Store_Worldwide-5) The song was written by Taggart, Halsey, [Shaun Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Frank "Shaun Frank"), [Freddy Kennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_the_Child_\(band\) "Louis the Child (band)"), [Isaac Slade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Slade "Isaac Slade") and [Joe King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_King_\(guitarist\) "Joe King (guitarist)"). Halsey's vocals were produced by [DJ Swivel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Swivel "DJ Swivel"),[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) while the main song production was handled by the Chainsmokers as usual. Musically, it is a [future bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_bass "Future bass") and [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop") song with a "[retro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro_\(music\) "Retro (music)")" style synthesizer in the chorus. Taggart and Halsey take turns singing their parts before singing the chorus together as the song concludes. The song is also included on the Japanese edition of The Chainsmokers' debut studio album, *[Memories...Do Not Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memories...Do_Not_Open "Memories...Do Not Open")* (2017).

In the United States, "Closer" became both the Chainsmokers' and Halsey's first number one single on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). The song stayed at the top spot for 12 consecutive weeks; it was the highest-charting [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") song to crack the *Billboard* Decade-End in the 2010s according to *Billboard*. The Chainsmokers became the first act to have four songs ("Closer" being the fourth) that top the [Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Electronic_Songs "Dance/Electronic Songs") chart, passing [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris"), who held the previous record with three. Internationally the single topped the charts in seventeen countries including Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Ireland, and the United Kingdom, making it both the Chainsmokers' and Halsey's first chart-topping song in all six countries. The song went on to become the first song to spend 26 weeks in the top five of the *Billboard* Hot 100 chart.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) It also became the second song in the history of the Hot 100 chart to spend 32 weeks in the top ten of the chart.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

The song was performed live for the first time at the Number Fest Concert at [Ohio University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_University "Ohio University") on Saturday April 16, 2016\.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) The Chainsmokers performed “Closer” for the second time at [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_\(festival\) "Coachella (festival)") on Sunday, April 17, 2016\. Halsey and the Chainsmokers performed the track live at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards") as well as a remix of the song at the 2016 [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"). Its music video was released on October 24, 2016\.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It received a nomination for [Best Pop Duo/Group Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Duo/Group_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance") at the [2017 Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards").

In 2018, the song received a diamond certification by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") for selling 10 million units in the United States, later being certified 18× Platinum in 2026\.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) In 2023, the Chainsmokers collaborated with Japanese rock star [Yoshiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoshiki_\(musician\) "Yoshiki (musician)") to perform a classical version of "Closer" in the documentary film *[Yoshiki: Under the Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoshiki:_Under_the_Sky "Yoshiki: Under the Sky")*.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

## Background and release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

The song's beat was created in a session between Chainsmokers member Andrew Taggart and Freddy Kennett of [Louis the Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_the_Child_\(band\) "Louis the Child (band)"). Taggart wrote the song with Canadian DJ [Shaun Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Frank "Shaun Frank") in one session, and Frank encouraged him to sing on the song. According to Taggart, the track was inspired by the [Blink-182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182 "Blink-182") song "[I Miss You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Miss_You_\(Blink-182_song\) "I Miss You (Blink-182 song)")", which the duo were listening to on repeat and is referenced in the song.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Lauren_Nostro-15) He later said the song instead was "[Feeling This](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feeling_This "Feeling This")", though he could not really remember which: "I've listened to their [self-titled album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182_\(album\) "Blink-182 (album)") so many times the whole thing is pretty much beat," he tweeted.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) The band [Taking Back Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taking_Back_Sunday "Taking Back Sunday") also influenced the song.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Lauren_Nostro-15) The song is about a couple who broke up and unexpectedly meet long after, leading to romantic attraction again.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) Before [Halsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halsey_\(singer\) "Halsey (singer)") was brought on as the female vocalist, the collaboration was originally supposed to feature former [Fifth Harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Harmony "Fifth Harmony") member [Camila Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camila_Cabello "Camila Cabello").[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

The song was mixed by [Jordan Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Swivel "DJ Swivel") who also oversaw the recording of the guest vocal.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

After comparisons were drawn between "Closer" and [The Fray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fray "The Fray")'s "[Over My Head (Cable Car)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Over_My_Head_\(Cable_Car\) "Over My Head (Cable Car)")", lead singer [Isaac Slade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Slade "Isaac Slade") and guitarist [Joe King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_King_\(guitarist\) "Joe King (guitarist)") of The Fray were credited as co-writers of "Closer" on September 2, 2016\.[\[20\]](#cite_note-Fekadu-20) The song was released on July 29, 2016, through [Disruptor Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disruptor_Records "Disruptor Records") and [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"). [Genius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genius_\(website\) "Genius (website)") pointed out the similarity between "Closer" and [Fetty Wap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetty_Wap "Fetty Wap")'s "[679](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/679_\(song\) "679 (song)")" in September 2016, claiming that the songs' choruses are nearly identical, with the only major difference being that Fetty's is in D major and The Chainsmokers' is in A-flat major. Genius even cut together a video of the choruses playing over each other.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

## Composition and lyrics

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition and lyrics")\]

The song is written in the key of [A-flat major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-flat_major "A-flat major") with a [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_time "Common time") tempo of 95 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute") and a chord progression of D♭(9)–E♭6add4–Fm7–E♭. The vocals span from E♭2 to B♭5.[\[22\]](#cite_note-Musicnotes-22)

The title of the song comes from part of the main hook: the singer asks his lover to "pull them *closer*" in the car's backseat. The words to the song speak to "youth" and "heartbreak".[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) The song makes references to [Range Rover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_Rover "Range Rover") vehicles, the cities of [Boulder, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulder,_Colorado "Boulder, Colorado"), [Tucson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona "Tucson, Arizona"), [Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona") and the band [Blink-182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182 "Blink-182").[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) It talks about being broke and passionate.\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

[Matt Medved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Medved "Matt Medved") of *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* wrote the song "sounds like an instant classic," stating that it "\[boasts\] an earworm chorus and evocative verses like 'play that [Blink-182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182 "Blink-182") song that we beat to death in [Tucson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona "Tucson, Arizona"),' (one of Halsey's few solo verses), "Closer" captures the [millennial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials "Millennials") [zeitgeist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeitgeist "Zeitgeist") in brilliantly infectious fashion."[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") journalist Deepa Lakshmin called the song "an upbeat, dance-worthy jam that deserves a spot on your summer playlist. It'll make you forget about all your pesky life problems and live in the moment."[\[26\]](#cite_note-26) The song received a more mixed review from *[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")*, with a consensus from various editors resulting in a 5/10 rating.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) While reviewing Halsey's 2021 album *[If I Can't Have Love, I Want Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Can't_Have_Love,_I_Want_Power "If I Can't Have Love, I Want Power")*, Dani Blum of *[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_\(website\) "Pitchfork (website)")* described their[\[note 1\]](#cite_note-28) "[Auto-Tuned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auto-Tune "Auto-Tune")" part of the song as the "ache \[...\] that threatened to define their career."[\[28\]](#cite_note-29)

*[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* ranked "Closer" at number 29 on their "100 Best Pop Songs of 2016" list: "The year's longest-running No. 1 on the Hot 100 was as predictable a smash as they come: Perfectly played duet drama, an immediately recognizable hook – maybe a little too instantly recognizable – and a Blink-182 reference that made every Millennial listening nod with begrudging respect. Overplay might've done The Chainsmokers and Halsey a temporary disservice, but just wait for the emotional rush that hits in 2025 when you're hanging in a hotel bar and hear this for the first time in years."[\[29\]](#cite_note-30)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Calvin_Harris_-_Rock_in_Rio_Madrid_2012_-_09.jpg/250px-Calvin_Harris_-_Rock_in_Rio_Madrid_2012_-_09.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Calvin_Harris_-_Rock_in_Rio_Madrid_2012_-_09.jpg)

[Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris") (*pictured*) had three songs that topped *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")*'s [Hot Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Dance/Electronic_Songs "Hot Dance/Electronic Songs") chart; "Closer" became the Chainsmoker's fourth song to do so and break the record.

"Closer" debuted at number nine on the *Billboard* Hot 100 in the issue dated August 20, 2016\.[\[30\]](#cite_note-31) It became the third top ten single for the Chainsmokers on the chart, after "[Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roses_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Roses (The Chainsmokers song)")" and "[Don't Let Me Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Let_Me_Down_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Don't Let Me Down (The Chainsmokers song)")". It is Halsey's first top ten on the chart and their second top forty. In the issue dated September 3, 2016, the song moved from number six to one, becoming both artists' first number-one song and the first song by a duo to top the chart since [Macklemore & Ryan Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macklemore_&_Ryan_Lewis "Macklemore & Ryan Lewis")' "[Thrift Shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrift_Shop "Thrift Shop")" and "[Can't Hold Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Hold_Us "Can't Hold Us")" in 2013\.[\[31\]](#cite_note-YM1-32)[\[32\]](#cite_note-Billboard1-33) It is also the first song titled "Closer" to reach number one ([Ne-Yo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ne-Yo "Ne-Yo")'s [song of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(Ne-Yo_song\) "Closer (Ne-Yo song)") reached number 7 in 2008). Moreover, the song also topped the [Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Electronic_Songs "Dance/Electronic Songs") chart, becoming the first song to reach number one on both the Hot 100 and the Dance/Electronic chart simultaneously since [Baauer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baauer "Baauer")'s "[Harlem Shake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem_Shake_\(song\) "Harlem Shake (song)")" in early 2013\.[\[31\]](#cite_note-YM1-32) It became the duo's fourth number one song to top the latter chart, passing [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris")' previous record of three songs.[\[32\]](#cite_note-Billboard1-33) It went on to top the Hot 100 chart for twelve consecutive weeks.[\[33\]](#cite_note-34)

On the issue date November 5, 2016, "Closer" became the 33rd song to top the chart for at least 10 weeks. By spending an 11th week atop the chart, it became the longest number one single of 2016 surpassing [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)")'s "[One Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Dance "One Dance")" which spent 10 non-consecutive weeks at number one. In its fourth week, the song was joined by [Twenty One Pilots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty_One_Pilots "Twenty One Pilots")' "[Heathens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heathens_\(Twenty_One_Pilots_song\) "Heathens (Twenty One Pilots song)")", which moved from number three to number two. This marks the first time (and the third time overall) that duos have held the top two spots at the same time since June 1985, when [Tears for Fears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tears_for_Fears "Tears for Fears") was on top with "[Everybody Wants to Rule the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody_Wants_to_Rule_the_World "Everybody Wants to Rule the World")" and [Wham!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wham! "Wham!") was number two with "[Everything She Wants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everything_She_Wants "Everything She Wants")." (The week before, the two songs were in the opposite order.)[\[34\]](#cite_note-YM-35) On the chart issue dated November 26, 2016, the song was ousted from number one by "[Black Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Beatles "Black Beatles")" by [Rae Sremmurd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rae_Sremmurd "Rae Sremmurd") featuring [Gucci Mane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gucci_Mane "Gucci Mane"). On the issue dated January 28, 2017, "Closer" surpassed [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber")'s "[Love Yourself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Yourself "Love Yourself")" for the most weeks logged in the top 10 from a song's debut, having totaled all 32 of its weeks on the chart in the region since its debut on the issue dated August 20, 2016\.[\[35\]](#cite_note-36)

On the issue dated March 11, 2017, "Closer" became the 4th song to stay in the top ten for 30 weeks. Only [Leann Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leann_Rimes "Leann Rimes")' "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")", [Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santana_\(band\) "Santana (band)")'s 1999 single "[Smooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_\(Santana_song\) "Smooth (Santana song)")" (feat. [Rob Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Thomas_\(musician\) "Rob Thomas (musician)")) and [Mark Ronson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ronson "Mark Ronson")'s "[Uptown Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")" (feat. [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars")) have achieved this feat since the *Billboard* Hot 100 was formed in 1958\. On the issue dated March 25, 2017, "Closer" spent its 32nd week in the top ten, tying [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes")' all-time record with "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")", before finally dropping out the following week. The record was broken later that year by [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran")'s "[Shape of You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shape_of_You "Shape of You")", which spent 33 consecutive weeks in the top ten.[\[36\]](#cite_note-37) The song's long run within the top 10 caused it to place at number 7 on [*Billboard'*s 2017 year-end chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2017 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2017") after placing at number 10 [the previous year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2016 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2016"), making "Closer" one of only four songs in the history of the chart to be ranked on the top ten of two separate Hot 100 year-end charts, along with [Chubby Checker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chubby_Checker "Chubby Checker")'s "[The Twist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twist_\(song\) "The Twist (song)")" (#10 in 1960 and \#9 in 1962), [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John")'s "[Candle in the Wind 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind_1997 "Candle in the Wind 1997")" (#1 in 1997 and \#8 in 1998), and [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes")' "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")" (#9 in 1997 and \#5 in 1998).

"Closer" achieved its 12th week atop [Digital Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Songs "Digital Songs") with 84,000 downloads sold in the week ending October 27, according to Nielsen Music; the total is the lowest for a number one song on the tally in 10 years.[\[37\]](#cite_note-ussales-38) The track became the third best-selling song of the year, behind [Flo Rida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flo_Rida "Flo Rida")'s "[My House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_House_\(Flo_Rida_song\) "My House (Flo Rida song)")" and [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake")'s "[Can't Stop the Feeling!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Stop_the_Feeling! "Can't Stop the Feeling!")".[\[38\]](#cite_note-sales-39)

Internationally, the song reached number one in Australia on August 13, 2016, also becoming both the Chainsmokers' and Halsey's first number-one song there.[\[39\]](#cite_note-AUS-40) It also peaked at number one in the UK, New Zealand and Canada. The song topped the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") for four weeks, becoming the first song by a duo to log multiple weeks at number one in both the US and the UK since [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO "LMFAO")'s "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")" in 2011\.[\[34\]](#cite_note-YM-35)

"Closer" is currently the [fifteenth most streamed song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_streamed_songs_on_Spotify "List of most streamed songs on Spotify") on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"). On May 19, 2017, it became only the second song to achieve 1 billion streams on the streaming platform. In April 2021, "Closer" surpassed 2 billion streams on Spotify, making it the sixth song to do so.[\[40\]](#cite_note-41)

## Lyric video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Lyric video")\]

The [lyric video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyric_video "Lyric video") for "Closer" was edited and directed by [Rory Kramer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rory_Kramer "Rory Kramer"), and features Alyssa Lynch and Jordan Wright. It received one billion views on January 10, 2017, and two billion views on February 4, 2018, making it the first lyric video ever to reach these milestones. As of January 2026, it has received over 3\.3 billion views, and is among the [fifty most-viewed videos of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos").[\[41\]](#cite_note-42)
